- Channel 0 (agent) is almost flat except for row 8, the bottom playable row. The largest weights are at row 8, columns 1 and 8: `(r8,c1)=8.24`, `(r8,c8)=9.73`, with nearby values `(r8,c2)=5.33`, `(r8,c7)=5.95`. This strongly suggests the agent is confined to the bottom row and its horizontal position matters.
- Channel 1 (moving objects) has large weights throughout the interior rows 2â7, across many columns. Examples: `(r4,c3)=17.41`, `(r4,c1)=15.48`, `(r4,c7)=16.12`, `(r3,c5)=15.29`. This looks like a moving object, such as a ball, that can be anywhere in the play area.
- Channel 2 (reward targets) has large weights only in the top rows 1â3. Examples: `(r3,c1)=6.06`, `(r3,c7)=6.20`, `(r2,c7)=3.68`, `(r1,c7)=3.06`. This suggests static reward objects arranged near the top of the grid.
- Channel 3 (obstacles) is high mainly on the outer border: `(r0,c6)=0.75`, `(r4,c0)=0.73`, `(r4,c9)=0.70`, `(r9,c9)=0.69`, while the interior is low. This matches only the wall border being an obstacle.
- Channel 4 (previous frame) is large in the middle/lower rows, e.g. `(r7,c4)=19.87`, `(r7,c5)=18.67`, `(r6,c4)=14.35`, and also has moderate values along row 8, e.g. `(r8,c1)=3.18`. This is consistent with the previous positions of a moving ball plus the bottom-row agent/paddle.
- Many top W1 connections are to channel 1 and channel 4 in the interior, channel 2 in the top rows, and channel 0 at row 8, e.g. unit 13 has `(r8,c8,ch0)=-4.701`; unit 15 has `(r8,c1,ch0)=4.066`; many units have strong weights from `(r4,c3,ch1)`, `(r7,c4,ch4)`, etc. The output layer is omitted, but the first-layer structure already implies horizontal control of a bottom-row paddle.

Reasoning:
The agent is fixed to the bottom row, so games where the agent moves freely around the gridâPac-Man, Snake, Sokoban, Froggerâare ruled out. The moving object is spread through the interior, while reward targets are static and concentrated in the top rows. Obstacles are essentially just the wall border. This is exactly the structure of Breakout: a paddle at the bottom, a ball moving through the play area, and bricks arranged in rows near the top. Pong would have paddles on the sides, not a bottom-row agent. Catch would not have static top-row reward targets. Space Invaders would put both moving objects and reward targets near the top, not a ball-like moving object throughout the interior.

Game:
Breakout, specifically a simplified/grid version of Atari Breakout.

Description:
The agent controls a paddle along the bottom row, moving left or right to bounce a ball upward and destroy bricks in the top rows for reward.

Confidence:
97%
